reason: council-remediation-2026-07-20 agent-R: original question cited Rule VIII Sec. 804 court dimensions, which is off-scope for an article limited to PD 1096 Rule I (General Provisions, Sec. 101-106). Replaced with a Rule I Sec. 106 definition question that the article directly supports.

source_audit_support.citation: PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Rule I, Section 106

proposed.text: Per IRR Sec. 106, an owner encloses an existing open terrace to create a new room, adding gross floor area without increasing building height. Under the Section 106 definitions, how is this work classified?

options.text: Alteration, because the building height is unchanged
Addition, because the work increases the floor area of the existing building
Renovation, because the visual appearance and value of the property are improved
Conversion, because the use of the terrace has been changed

proposed.rationale: Section 106 defines an addition as new construction that increases the height or floor area of an existing building or structure. Adding gross floor area by enclosing a terrace meets the addition definition even when building height is unchanged; the floor-area increase is the controlling element.
proposed.explanation: Section 106 distinguishes addition (increase in height or floor area) from alteration (changes without height/floor-area increase), renovation (value/appearance improvement), and conversion (change in use or occupancy).
proposed.code_citation: PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Rule I, Section 106
